sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The path was flat through FY2022, then stepped up 17.7% in FY2023 and 17.3% in FY2026 [D280][D421].
The FY2023 step came from the Cerner acquisition, which contributed revenue across all three businesses [P48].
The FY2026 step came from cloud revenues as customers purchased applications and infrastructure technologies and renewed cloud contracts [P17].
Cloud Infrastructure contributed 13.7pp of the 17.3% revenue growth in FY2026 and reached 26.9% of revenue [D645][D421][D643].
Cloud applications and cloud infrastructure contributed 16% and 84% of constant-currency cloud revenue growth in FY2026 [P17].
The Americas contributed 14.2pp of FY2026 growth and 66.0% of revenue [D470][D468].
Operating income grew 16.6% in FY2026 against 17.3% revenue growth, an incremental margin of 29.4% [D422][D421][D442].
Operating costs grew 0.3pp faster than revenue in FY2026, at 17.7% [D443][D436].
Operating margin of 30.6% in FY2026 sits below the 32.2% window median and well below the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
The FY2026 margin slipped 0.2pp as R&D added 1.9pp while other lines took off 2.1pp [D433][D444][D445].
The other-line drag reflects a $1.5 billion rise in restructuring and other expenses from the 2026 Restructuring Plan [P11].
In FY2026 net margin of 25.2% sat 5.4pp below the 30.6% operating margin, narrower than the 9.1pp gap in FY2025 [F54][F34][D832][D831].
Operating cash flow of $32.0 billion was 1.88x net income in FY2026, above the 1.58x window median [F84][D408][D822].
Operating cash rose $11.2 billion on higher net income and favorable working capital, including $4.6 billion of customer prepayments [P6].
Free cash flow was -$23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin, as capex of $55.7 billion reached 82.6% of revenue and 7.30x D&A [F104][D405][F94][D404][D410].
Investing outflows rose $30.1 billion mainly on a $34.4 billion increase in capital expenditures [P5].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion in FY2026, net cash of -145.0% of revenue against a -0.5% peer median, the 0th percentile of six peers [D414][D415][D816][D815].
Debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion on $42.7 billion of senior notes issued in FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $5.9 billion were paid while free cash flow was -$23.7 billion, and the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D416][F104][D438].
The balance sheet now carries the data-center build rather than funding it from internal cash, and $260 billion of additional lease commitments sit off balance sheet [P1].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover 1.3 years of the FY2026 burn [D412][D419].
The burn is a capex choice rather than an operating shortfall, but the cushion against it is now thin [R1].
Free cash flow ran below net income in FY2025 and FY2026, at -0.03x and -1.39x [D362][D409].
Two years of sub-net-income conversion mark a break from the 1.06x window median [D800].
Net debt rose for a second year to $97.6 billion and total debt rose 39.9% in FY2026 [D414][D440].
Leverage is compounding alongside the capex cycle, so the 0th-percentile net cash position is the number to watch [D815].
Whether FY2027 capex falls below the FY2026 $55.7 billion, reported in the FY2027 10-K cash flow statement [F94].
Whether free cash flow margin recovers above the -35.2% FY2026 low toward the 26.0% window median [D792][D794].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue improves from -145.0% in FY2026 [D415].
